text:
marie (product): quick sync — ACME flagged that CompetitorX now ships per-tenant routing + granular pricing tiers. they asked for parity. do we treat as table-stakes or double down on our differentiated story? :thinking_face:

alex (eng): can you paste the ask? is it just routing+pricing or also UI for self-serve tiers?

marie (product): mainly routing control (route by region/tier/fallback) + a pricing API so enterprise customers can map usage to internal chargeback. they want self-serve if possible. ben (sales) pulled it into the renewal convo.

ben (sales): acme's renewal is in 6 weeks. if we don't show a plan they will request a discount. they care about: predictable latency per-tenant, ability to route to lower-cost model variants during bursts, and a single billing hook.

ryan (eng-runtime): technically we already support model routing and per-tenant weights in Dedicated, but not as a self-serve productized control plane. exposing it safely + with quotas is doable but not trivial. rough estimate: 6–8w to productize with tests + rollout automation.

anya (design): UX asks: 1) admin UI for tenant routing 2) templated presets for common patterns 3) clear warnings for SLA changes when routing to cheaper models. I can do mocks in 1 week if we prioritise. :white_check_mark:

sam (growth): signal-wise, parity would reduce churn risk on enterprise pilots, but we should avoid turning into a copycat. can we attach a positioning narrative: “flex routing for predictable economics” that leans into our cost controls?

alex (eng): technical constraints to call out: batching/kv cache invalidation when you split traffic across models, cross-tenant cache safety, and metric continuity for evals. need canonical fallback policy semantics.

ryan (eng-runtime): proposed engineering scope split: (A) enable per-route policy config + RBAC (B) billing hook + metering events (C) admin UI + templates (D) rollout + canary. estimate by bucket: A 3w, B 2w, C 1–2w (design dependent), D 1w ops. total ≈ 7–8w.

marie (product): OK — options: 1) Fast parity: ship A+B minimal APIs (no UI), offer Professional Services to set it up — 6w to show plan to acme. 2) Full product: A+B+C+D — 8w and immediate GA. 3) Defer and counter with differentiator: invest 4w building a “cost-sla policy” that routes by cost+latency signal (more opinionated, harder to match CompetitorX but more differentiating).

ben (sales): acme will accept a PS-based short term if we commit to a roadmap date in writing. they prefer full product but will settle for minimal if we promise self-serve in next quarter.

anya (design): if we go fast-parity (option 1), I'll prioritize admin API docs and a minimal control panel mock for the PS team.

sam (growth): we should pair any parity commit with a public positioning post highlighting our cost controls > competitors. that reduces perception of being just parity.

alex (eng): can we define launch criteria? my suggestion: - infra: route policies supported with 99.9% success on test harness - latency p95 impact < 10% vs baseline - billing events emitted for every routed request - RBAC for tenant admins in place

ryan (eng-runtime): add regression criteria: no KV cache correctness regressions in canary; end-to-end smoke tests for model fallback sequences.

marie (product): draft launch criteria (to decide now): 1) Minimal API shipped & documented (A+B) 2) Success signals in canary with a real tenant (acme) for 2 weeks 3) Rolling deploy with automatic fallback policy 4) Exec signoff on pricing hook. If we hit that, we commit to self-serve UI in next sprint.

ben (sales): sounds good. can we promise the 6w plan in writing? i need the timeline to include the PS setup window.

alex (eng): i can commit to the A+B 6w plan if we freeze scope: no UI, no templating, only API + default fallback policy + metering. engineering caveat: may need a short hotfix week after canary.

sam (growth): marketing note: call it “Tenant Routing & Chargeback API — early access”. do not frame as parity.

anya (design): will ship the minimal docs + 1-page admin mock for PS by EOW.

marie (product): decision: we go option 1 (fast parity) with a clear public narrative framing cost controls as the reason. action items: @alex scope freeze + eng plan; @ryan canary plan; @anya deliver mock+docs; @ben close communication to acme with the plan. i'll draft the commit email.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: canary routing-api v0.1 -> staging at 3160016000.

alex (eng): tagging follow-ups: - add telemetry tag "route_policy.version" - add e2e tests for fallback sequences - schedule 2h on-call window for canary week.

ben (sales): i'll ask acme for a 2-week canary start window next Tue.

marie (product): thanks all. we'll reconvene after the first canary week. :pray:
